players.product: KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) anti-PD-1 therapy; intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157), jointly developed with Moderna

quarterly_data.signal: 10-Q: first-half 2026 sales were $32,893 million (first half 2025: $31,335 million); Keytruda/Keytruda Qlex $16,400 million (+8%), including Keytruda Qlex $590 million; Winrevair $1,114 million (+81%); Gardasil/Gardasil 9 $2,238 million (first half 2025: $2,453 million); Animal Health $3,566 million (+10%). First-half capital expenditures were $1,884 million (first half 2025: $2,092 million), lower in part because of the 2025 acquisition of a facility from WuXi Vaccines.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 sales $32,893 million; Keytruda/Keytruda Qlex $16,400 million (+8%); H1 capex $1,884 million

quarterly_data.signal: 10-Q collaborations and exclusivity: under the amended Koselugo agreement Merck received $150 million in Q1 2026 and $50 million of regulatory milestones from AstraZeneca in Q2 2026, with $50 million due in Q3 2027 and $75 million in Q3 2028, and receives tiered royalties of 6% to 7% on net sales. On June 12, 2026 AstraZeneca and Merck received a second Paragraph IV notice from Cipla seeking approval of generic Lynparza tablets; they filed a patent infringement lawsuit in July 2026, and the FDA will stay approval of Cipla's second ANDA for 30 months unless an adverse court decision comes earlier. Merck had capitalized a net $226 million of shared facility costs for the intismeran autogene collaboration with Moderna at June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Koselugo $50 million milestone received Q2 2026; royalties 6% to 7%; Cipla second Paragraph IV notice June 12, 2026
